quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Think about what your mouth is doing during the target sound in "crash". Does it raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice? Or does it raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on?
quests.explanation: This is /k/, not /g/: in "crash", you raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice. The distractor would instead need raising the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on, which changes the sound completely.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Try producing "carve" yourself. To make /v/, you rest your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow with your voice on — quite different from /f/, which needs you to rest your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow with no voice.

quests.hint: Here's the key contrast in "chin": /tʃ/ is made by stopping the air just behind your top teeth, then releasing it as a hiss, with no voice, and /ʃ/ is made by rounding your lips slightly and pushing air across your tongue with no voice. Which description fits what you hear?
quests.explanation: In "chin", the target sound is /tʃ/, made by stopping the air just behind your top teeth, then releasing it as a hiss, with no voice. The distractor /ʃ/ would instead require you to round your lips slightly and push air across your tongue with no voice — a clearly different sound once you isolate it.
